answers: Most teens don't find music history in their dad's stuff, but Maggie Poukkula's dad is Seattle musician Tony Poukkula, who was a friend of Kurt Cobain. Her find? Photos of Nirvana's first concert, performed by then 20-year-old Cobain and his new band in March 1987 in Tony Poukkula's basement. "My dad showed me them awhile back, but he never mentioned that's what was going on in the photos," Maggie Poukkula, 19, tells Rolling Stone. "I found out because of all the articles. I didn't realize it was such a historical thing. I thought they were just cool pictures of my dad and Kurt jamming together." She tweeted the photos last week, and the post quickly went viral. That first concert featured the early Nirvana lineup of Cobain, bassist Krist Novoselic, and drummer Aaron Burckhard playing original songs and Led Zeppelin covers. Similar early-days footage of Cobain and Co. featured in the recent documentary Montage of Heck has renewed interest in the grunge band. The Emmy-nominated project includes home movies, never-before-heard music, and intimate interviews with Cobain's family and friends, notes SPIN. After being critically acclaimed at festivals across the country, the film will return to theaters on Aug. 7, adds Rolling Stone. (Want a little more Cobain history? Here's the mix tape he made at 21.)

full.prediction:
**Summary of News Passages**

Recent news has highlighted the discovery of rare photographs from Nirvana's first concert in March 1987, shared by Maggie Poukkula, the 19-year-old daughter of Tony Poukkula, a member of the Seattle band Laytem. Poukkula, who grew up with Kurt Cobain and hosted Nirvana's first show in his basement, recently tweeted a photo strip featuring three snapshots from the 1987 gig in Raymond, Washington. The images, which she initially thought were just of her father and Cobain jamming together, were later identified as significant historical artifacts. The photos were found tucked away in her father's biographies of Cobain and Nirvana.

The concert featured Nirvana's early lineup—Kurt Cobain, Krist Novoselic, and Aaron Burckhard—with Poukkula reportedly joining the band on guitar for two Led Zeppelin covers. An incomplete set list from the show includes covers of "Heartbreaker" and "How Many More Times," as well as early versions of songs like "Aero Zeppelin" and "If You Must." A recording of the "Heartbreaker" jam was included in the 2004 box set *With the Lights Out*, and a bootleg version of "If You Must" is available on YouTube.

This discovery follows a wave of rare Cobain and Nirvana artifacts, many of which were featured in Brett Morgen's documentary *Montage of Heck*. The film, which provided unprecedented access to Cobain's archives, includes notebooks, audio cassettes, and other materials that offer insight into the band's early years. The documentary has been well-received and is set to return to movie theaters starting August 7th.

In a separate news update, the Internet Archive has launched an initiative to address broken links on the web. The project, known as "No More 404," aims to archive pages as they are created and preserve the pages they reference. This ensures that even if a page is changed or removed, a link to the version that was live when the page was written will be preserved. The goal is to fix all broken links and provide users with access to the original content intended by the page's authors. This effort is part of a broader campaign to maintain the integrity of online information and improve the user experience on the web.
